claims.statement: The pinned personal-instructions note limits that feature to Copilot Chat on GitHub. It is a historical surface-specific claim, not proof of support in IDEs, current availability, instruction obedience, or adopted project policy.

The plan-agent introduction describes read-only research and codebase analysis, actionable decomposition with open questions, and a concise iterative plan for user review. It states no code changes before user approval and permits approved-plan handoff or saving. Its assurance that requirements are considered is not proof of complete requirements coverage or enforced sandboxing; source text is not an approval receipt.

The plan steps describe iterative review/questions and distinguish Start Implementation, which launches implementation in agent mode, from Open in Editor, which launches an agent session to generate Markdown plan details for manual work or saving. Open in Editor is therefore not described as merely viewing a passive file; neither path was invoked and no implementation approval is inferred.

The usage note warns that additional usage may be capped and recommends upgrading after exhausting plan AI credits. This is an upstream recommendation, not guaranteed overage availability, a measured remaining quota, or authorization for a paid upgrade.

The pinned credit table and variable definitions describe Pro at 10 USD monthly with 1000 base plus 500 flex totaling 1500 credits; Pro Plus at 39 USD with 3900 plus 3100 totaling 7000; and Max at 100 USD with 10000 plus 10000 totaling 20000. Each displayed sum is consistent. These historical source values are not live prices, a complete billing contract, entitlement verification, or purchase approval.

The enterprise-trial note requires conversion from a GitHub Enterprise Cloud trial to a paid enterprise before purchasing Copilot. This historical purchase prerequisite is not authority to convert or incur charges, nor a finding that the user's enterprise is currently in a trial.
